name: 8-Chlorotheophylline

tolerance.full: Tolerance develops with repeated use, similar to caffeine

addictionPotential: low addiction potential with minimal abuse liability
toxicities: May cause cardiac issues at high doses, especially when combined with diphenhydramine in dimenhydrinate
summary: 8-Chlorotheophylline is a xanthine-class stimulant chemically and functionally similar to caffeine. It is primarily used as a wakefulness-promoting agent in dimenhydrinate to counteract the sedative effects of diphenhydramine.
effectsSummary: Stimulation, increased wakefulness, increased heart rate, potential cardiac stress at high doses, especially when combined with diphenhydramine.
dosageRemark: Usually not taken alone; found in fixed combination with diphenhydramine as dimenhydrinate. Individual dosing is not well established.
generalRisks: May cause cardiac issues at high doses. When combined with diphenhydramine (as in dimenhydrinate), may lead to severe tachycardia.
longtermRisks: Limited data on long-term risks. As a xanthine derivative, chronic high intake may lead to similar issues as caffeine including anxiety, sleep disturbances, and cardiovascular strain.
saferUse: Avoid high doses when taken as part of dimenhydrinate
Be aware of the combined effects with diphenhydramine
Monitor heart rate if using regularly
